caption: The drawing shows a top-down view of a homestead garden, labeled "CHEESEBROUGH HOMESTEAD" on a yellow ribbon at the bottom. At the center, there is a rectangular reddish-brown building with a cross-shaped footprint, surrounded by a light beige or tan path that winds throughout the property. Surrounding the building are green areas with clusters of trees depicted in various shades of green. To the upper left of the main building, there is a rectangular patterned garden made up of green, yellow, red, and white sections organized with geometric symmetry, and labeled "NORTH" with an arrow. Directly above the main path, there is a circular flower bed filled with multi-colored patterns, with shrubbery nearby. At the far upper right, a smaller circular or hexagonal structure is present. The lower right portion shows an octagonal green-bordered area with a large tree at its center and a gazebo-like pergola structure covered in green vines and red flowers. The background is mostly dark green, indicating grass or foliage, and the entire layout is bordered by a beige or tan margin. The upper right corner has a label, "from BLACKWELL'S SURVEY."
title: Cheeseborough Estate
cluster: #12 — Spanish Colonial Art of the Southwest
